correctness.rationale: Disconnected four-sets have shore splits 4+0 (all), 3+1 (the singleton misses its matched vertex), or 2+2 (both matching edges are absent); these disjoint classes have 30, 120, 15 members. A face of the dual is exactly a set containing none of them. The separate exact replay builds the full face poset and reproduces 768 faces and 350 disjoint matching pairs; topological sorting all 2,832 covers in the match-reversed graph reaches all 768 nodes. With orientations by increasing vertex order, each signed pivot contributes −[u:f]/[u:t] to the other facet terms. Acyclicity makes the gradient recursion finite, and the 66 integral coefficients from the unique critical four-cell are all zero; mod-two ranks are not needed. Forman's theorem gives one vertex, 66 three-cells, one four-cell and no other cells. The three-skeleton is a wedge of 3-spheres, is 2-connected, and Hurewicz identifies its π3 with H3; the attaching map has the computed zero degree vector and is nullhomotopic. Alexander duality for 12 vertices takes degrees 4 and 3 to original reduced homology degrees 5 and 6 via 9−i, with ranks 1 and 66 and no torsion. Purity follows from equal complement sizes. The lower-dimensional field homology obstructs both pure shellability and Cohen–Macaulayness over every field.
residual_risks: This is a finite graph-specific computation. Only the dual has a full homotopy-type assertion; the original complex has an integral homology assertion.

value.rationale: The six-crown is the next crown after the inspected five-crown at the same natural cutoff, and the complete bipartite graph is a closely related benchmark. The exact example changes the pattern from a single reduced homology degree to two adjacent integer degrees, neither top-dimensional, and identifies an integral wedge for the dual rather than merely computing field Betti numbers. It supplies a specific useful test case for structural or computational predictions about cuts of crowns and matching deletions.
residual_risks: Does not imply recurrence in larger crowns, minimality of this example among all graphs, or the full homotopy type of the original cut complex.
